display.purpose: The page heading, once per sheet, on its own paper ground.

sounding.purpose: The title block's four figures. Never wraps between currency mark and figure; scales down instead.

title.purpose: Sheet heads, dialog titles, section heads.

body.purpose: Table content and form values, tabular figures on by default. Prose capped at 68ch.

note.purpose: Dates, due timings, placeholders, subtitles, sheet feet — anything that drifts.

label.purpose: Condensed tracked caps for column heads, nav section heads, field labels, legends.

chip.purpose: Status words only. Never used for anything that is not a state.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: The system's only elevation. Dialogs, the mobile nav drawer, and the signed-out login plate. A real offset cast, never a halo. Nothing in the document plane may use it.

motion.name: tide-redraw
motion.value: 520ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) — transform: scaleY(0) → scaleY(1), origin top
motion.purpose: The one authored moment. Recording a payment re-sounds the row: its depth band is redrawn top to bottom. Fires once, on the row whose payment status changed, and nowhere else.

motion.name: sounding-settle
motion.purpose: Shared entrance convention for overlaying surfaces (dialogs, popovers). A convention, not a second authored moment.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Background, colour and border only, on buttons, fields and checkboxes. No transform, no lift.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce → all animation and transition durations collapse to 0.01ms
motion.purpose: Global override; no motion is exempt.

narrative.overview:
An Admiralty chart is a dense field of numbers meant to be read at a glance, under pressure, in bad light. That is exactly this app's problem, so the app is built as a chart rather than as a dashboard. Amounts are soundings. Time-to-due is a charted depth. Overdue wears the chart's own restricted-area magenta. Land — navigation, headers, anything that is structure rather than data — is buff plate; the working field is open paper water. Nothing is rounded, nothing is striped, and nothing floats unless it genuinely floats.

The build's material is hairline rules on paper. Structure is drawn with a 1px ink border and separated with a 1px soft rule; there are no cards, no tinted panels with soft corners, and no shadow used decoratively. Type carries the chart's own convention literally: condensed tracked caps label features, italic names anything in the water (dates, timings, notes), and tabular figures are the soundings themselves. The single family, Archivo, supplies all three through its width and italic axes.

The system's discipline is chromatic restraint. Four status hues exist and each means one thing; the interface's own chrome — buttons, focus, checkboxes, active nav, sort marks, pagination — is ink and only ink. The loudest thing in any viewport must be a late invoice, never a control. The direction contract said "no elevation"; the build ships exactly one elevation token, used only where something genuinely floats above the sheet (dialogs, the mobile drawer, the signed-out plate). That divergence is recorded, not hidden: flat is the rule, and the one shadow is the named exception.
keyCharacteristics: Zero radius, enforced at the token level across the entire radius scale
Hairline ink rules as the only structural material; no card shadows
Four status colours, each with exactly one meaning, never used for chrome
Chart lettering: condensed tracked caps for features, italic for water, tabular figures for soundings
Status is never colour alone — a band, a word, and a legend

rules.name: The One Magenta Rule
rules.body: Caution magenta means overdue and nothing else. It is never a primary button, never a focus ring, never a checked box, never an active tab, never a selection tick. Two review rounds were spent reclaiming it from chrome; the audit test is one sentence — if a magenta mark on screen does not correspond to a late invoice, it is a bug.

rules.name: The Ink-Chrome Rule
rules.body: Every interactive affirmation in the app is ink: primary fill, focus outline, checked state, focused field border, active nav mark, current page, sort arrow. Chrome has no colour of its own.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor Rule
rules.body: ink-3 (#6b7069) and sand (#96660b) are not aesthetic choices; both were computed to clear 4.5:1 on paper (#fbfaf6) at body size. Do not lighten either. If a lighter tertiary tone is wanted, use less type, not paler type.

rules.name: The Never-Colour-Alone Rule
rules.body: No status is communicated by hue alone. Every depth band is accompanied by a worded chip, and the register carries a depth-key legend in its bottom margin naming all five bands.

rules.name: The Chart Lettering Rule
rules.body: Upright type names fixed things — invoice numbers, parties, amounts. Italic names things in the water — dates, timings, notes, anything that drifts. Choosing between them is a semantic decision, not a styling one.

rules.name: The Tabular Default Rule
rules.body: Tabular figures are set on body and on every field. Never turn them off in a numeric context; a register whose digits do not align has failed at its only job.

rules.name: The Prose-Off-The-Ruling Rule
rules.body: Prose is never read off a ruled surface. Headings, subtitles, footers and margin legends sit on their own paper ground even when they overlay the plotting field.

rules.name: The Coarser-Field Rule
rules.body: The app's plotting field is always coarser than the ruling of anything laid on it (88px field against 44px sheet ruling). If a new ruled surface approaches 88px, change the surface, not the field.

rules.name: The Sticky-Never-Doubles Rule
rules.body: The sticky bar names the sheet only after the H1 has scrolled out of view. The same words never appear twice in one viewport.

rules.name: The Flat-Sheet Rule
rules.body: Anything that lives in the document plane — sheets, wells, title blocks, tables, chips, buttons, fields — has no shadow. Depth is drawn, not lit. Lift is available only to portalled or overlaying surfaces.

rules.name: The Drawn-Depth Rule
rules.body: The one place the system genuinely expresses depth is the depth band, and that depth is semantic (time-to-due), not spatial.

rules.name: The First-Cell Rule
rules.body: The depth band goes on the row's first <td>, never on the <tr>. A positioned table row breaks cell layout in browsers; this shipped as a real bug on two pages before it was caught. Every consumer — register, customers, users, trash — applies depth depth-* to a cell.

dos: Do keep every interactive affirmation in ink — primary fill, focus outline, checked box, focused field border, active nav mark, current page, sort arrow.
Do pair every status colour with a word. Chips carry the status text; the register carries the depth-key legend.
Do put the depth band on the first <td>, never on the <tr>.
Do build containers from 1px hairlines: ink for a sheet's boundary, rule for internal separators, rule-soft for divisions inside a sheet.
Do choose upright versus italic semantically — upright for fixed things, italic for anything in the water.
Do keep tabular figures on in every numeric context.
Do set prose on its own paper ground whenever it overlays a ruled field.
Do keep the plotting field coarser than any ruling laid on it (88px field against 44px sheet ruling).
Do reserve Lift for surfaces that genuinely float — dialogs, the drawer, the signed-out plate.
Do route every modal through the single dialog primitive.
Do give navigation entries a chart symbol only alongside a text label.
donts: Don't use caution magenta for anything but overdue. Not a primary button, not a focus ring, not a checked box, not an active tab.
Don't lighten ink-3 or sand; both were computed against the 4.5:1 floor on paper.
Don't reintroduce corner radius. The whole scale is zeroed at the token level and a rounded-* utility will silently do nothing — if you find yourself reaching for one, the shape is wrong.
Don't add a shadow to anything in the document plane. Flat is the material, not a preference.
Don't add a second authored motion moment. settle is a convention; depth-tide is the one moment and it belongs to the payment event.
Don't use a chart symbol on an icon-only control. Recognition wins over grammar wherever there is no text label — that is why trash is a bin and not a wreck.
Don't set prose on the graticule or on any ruled surface.
Don't reintroduce floating metric tiles. The title block's ruled cell grid is the system's answer for summary figures.
Don't apply any of this system to src/components/templates/. The printed document is an excluded zone.
